_note: Machine-checkable form of the Deliverable Quality Bar in SKILL.md. The four types, the A-E answers, the five-and-five lists, artifacts, placement and robust decisions are code; so is the ban on ranking futures. Jev judges whether the logics differ in kind, whether Collapse shows people doing well, and the Handoff.

structural.bar: opens with a direct answer to the decision or question the user asked, which the rest of the output supports
structural.desc: the output opens with an Answer section

structural.bar: includes all four generic futures (Continued Growth, Collapse, Discipline, Transformation), each labelled with its type
structural.desc: the four futures are labelled Growth, Collapse, Discipline and Transformation

structural.bar: calls no future best, worst, or most likely, and describes Collapse with people who do well in it
structural.desc: no future is called best, worst or most likely

structural.bar: writes each future from inside, positively, with an artifact from that future
answers A–E for each future, with five things to do now toward (D) and five against (E)
answers A–E for each future, with five things to do now toward (D) and five against (E)
answers A–E for each future, with five things to do now toward (D) and five against (E)
structural.desc: five things toward (D) for each of four futures

structural.bar: answers A–E for each future, with five things to do now toward (D) and five against (E)
structural.desc: five things against (E) for each of four futures

structural.bar: places the subject in each future
structural.desc: the subject is placed in each future

structural.bar: names at least three design decisions that hold in all four futures
structural.desc: at least three robust design decisions

structural.bar: records trends and signals in the Evidence Ledger, each typed `user-supplied`, `sourced`, or `assumption`
records trends and signals in the Evidence Ledger, each typed `user-supplied`, `sourced`, or `assumption`
structural.desc: every ledger row is typed user-supplied, sourced or assumption

structural.bar: ends with a Handoff naming the next method and why

semantic.bar: gives each future a distinct underlying logic rather than a different level of the same variable
semantic.instructions: In `items[{i}]`, does each future rest on a different underlying logic, rather than being a different level of the same variable?

criteria.true: The futures differ in how the world works: for example growth through markets, a breakdown and local rebuilding, a deliberate limit on consumption, a technological change in what people are.
criteria.false: The futures are high, medium, low and very low settings of one thing, such as more or less adoption of the same technology.

semantic.bar: calls no future best, worst, or most likely, and describes Collapse with people who do well in it
semantic.instructions: Does the section in `items[{i}]` describe people who do well or find something good in this future?

criteria.true: Names people or groups who thrive, gain or find meaning in this future, even if others suffer.
criteria.false: Describes only loss, suffering or failure, with nobody doing well.

semantic.bar: ends with a Handoff naming the next method and why
semantic.instructions: Does the section in `items[{i}]` name a next method to use and give a reason for choosing it?

criteria.true: Names a method (for example fdbx-three-horizons, fdbx-causal-layered-analysis) and says what it would do with this output.
criteria.false: Names no method, or names one with no reason.
